memory.content: One implementation agent owns a PR until merge or cancel.
Never merge or production-release without explicit human approval.
First-run setup before inventing defaults: ask once for code host repo, ticket tracker project, product channel, staging channel, and CI branch. Create or update listeners only after those are named.
Importer must connect chat, ticket tracker, and code host before enabling listeners.

skills.name: Chat ticket intake
skills.description: Use when a product or staging chat asks to file a bug/feature or reports a failure that needs a ticket.
skills.content:
---
name: Chat ticket intake
description: >-
  Use when a product or staging chat asks to file a bug/feature or reports a
  failure that needs a ticket.
---
# Chat → ticket intake

When a user reports a bug, requests a feature, or an agent/runtime failure needs tracking:

1. Confirm the configured ticket tracker from first-run setup. Do not invent project keys.
2. Search open tickets for a duplicate (same symptom, component, or error signature).
3. If a match exists: add evidence (chat summary, repro steps, error text, links) and reply with the existing ticket id.
4. If none: create a ticket with a clear title, problem statement, acceptance-criteria stub, and a link back to the originating chat.
5. Reply in-thread with ticket id (and link if available). Stay quiet when nothing is actionable.

Never invent company names, private URLs, or tracker projects the importer has not configured.

skills.name: PR babysit one agent
skills.description: Use when implementing a ticket or babysitting one PR through review and CI with a single cloud coding agent.
skills.content:
---
name: PR babysit one agent
description: >-
  Use when implementing a ticket or babysitting one PR through review and CI
  with a single cloud coding agent.
---
# One agent owns the PR

When implementing a ticket or babysitting a change through review and CI:

1. Confirm ticket acceptance criteria and constraints before coding starts.
2. Launch or resume ONE cloud coding agent on the watched repo and branch. Do not fan out competing agents on the same change.
3. On new review comments or CI failure: send the findings to that same agent, wait for a push, then re-request review or recheck CI.
4. Surface only merge-ready state (CI green — human approval still required) or a real blocker. Skip unchanged “still waiting” noise.
5. Never merge or cut a production release without explicit human approval.

Keep one fingerprint of PR/ticket state so duplicate status pings stay silent.

skills.name: Staging verify report
skills.description: Use after a healthy staging deploy to verify the change and report what passed, failed, or could not be verified.
skills.content:
---
name: Staging verify report
description: >-
  Use after a healthy staging deploy to verify the change and report what
  passed, failed, or could not be verified.
---
# Staging verification

After a healthy staging deploy for the change under test:

1. Trigger only on a healthy staging deploy signal — not on speculative “maybe deployed.”
2. Exercise the changed behavior through the interfaces the product actually uses (API, agent tools, or UI path as the importer configured).
3. Report clearly: what passed, what failed, and what could not be verified (and why).
4. On failure: open or update a ticket, or send evidence back to the owning implementation agent.
5. Do not claim green without evidence. Local checks and live staging probes answer different questions — say which you ran.

Optional follow-up: if verification uncovers missing behavior, file a new ticket rather than silently expanding scope.
